title: First-order power series comparison for a complete local algebra over a field
statement: Let k be a field and A a complete Noetherian local k-algebra [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring, def-weil-pbc-adically-complete-ring], with maximal ideal m and residue field K. Let d be the minimal number of generators of m, let T=K[[X_1,...,X_d]] [def-weil-pbc-multivariate-power-series], and put N=(X_1,...,X_d). There is a surjective ring map g:A -> T/N^2 whose inverse image of the image of N is exactly m. No formal smoothness assumption is imposed.

source.place: Tag 07EI, construction of f_1; coefficient field from Algebra Tag 032A

proof.text: Apply the coefficient-subring theorem with the residue characteristic p. The algebra maps from k to A and its residue field are injective, so their characteristics agree. Thus p is zero in A; the coefficient subring maximal ideal generated by p is zero. The coefficient subring is a field and its residue isomorphism supplies a section s:K -> A.

The cotangent space m/m^2 is a finite-dimensional K-vector space since m is finitely generated. Choose a basis and representatives x_i in m. Nakayama says they generate m. Conversely every generating set spans the cotangent space after reduction, so the basis size is exactly d=m.spanFinrank.

Each class in A/m^2 is uniquely s(c)+sum_i s(c_i)x_i: reduction determines c and the cotangent basis determines the remaining coefficients. All products x_i*x_j vanish. This identifies the ring with K plus K^d, with multiplication (c,v)(c_prime,v_prime)=(c*c_prime,c*v_prime+c_prime*v).

Constant and linear coefficients give the same square-zero decomposition of T/N^2. A series with zero constant and linear terms lies in N^2: order the finite variable set, assign each monomial of degree at least two to its first two variable factors, remove those factors, and sum the finitely many X_i*X_j times the resulting series. The converse is immediate from the Cauchy product, which also gives the displayed multiplication.

Identify the two decompositions, taking the cotangent basis to the variables and fixing K. This gives a ring isomorphism A/m^2 -> T/N^2. Compose with the quotient of A to obtain the surjective map g. The image of N is exactly the zero-constant subspace, and the constant of g(a) is the residue of a, so its inverse image is m. For d=0, Nakayama gives m=0 and both quotients are K.

lean.statement:
theorem exists_firstOrder_powerSeries_comparison (k : Type u) (A : Type v)
    [Field k] [CommRing A] [Algebra k A] [IsNoetherianRing A] [IsLocalRing A]
    [IsAdicComplete (IsLocalRing.maximalIdeal A) A] :
    let T := MvPowerSeries (Fin (IsLocalRing.maximalIdeal A).spanFinrank)
      (IsLocalRing.ResidueField A)
    let N : Ideal T := Ideal.span (Set.range (fun i ↦ (MvPowerSeries.X i : T)))
    ∃ g : A →+* T ⧸ N ^ 2,
      Function.Surjective g ∧
      (N.map (Ideal.Quotient.mk (N ^ 2))).comap g =
        IsLocalRing.maximalIdeal A
